newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to form group on future Eurobond issue.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to form group on future Eurobond issue.

text.p: The Finance Ministry and central bank plan to set up a working group to prepare the former Soviet republic's first Eurobond issue, officials said on Thursday.
Alexei Berezhnoi, a senior Finance Ministry official, told Reuters the group would be made up of specialists from the ministry, central bank and other organisations.
He said the group "will work out recommendations and conditions, the size and time frame for Ukraine's issue of securities on foreign markets."

But Berezhnoi gave no further details on what form the initial issues could take. He said any bond issue required amendments to existing laws on securities, which made no provision for bond issues outside the country.
Berezhnoi said Ukraine had yet to choose foreign firms to help it launch the bond issue.
Earlier this month, Ukrinform Business News quoted central bank official Oleh Rubachuk as saying several Western banks were taking part in a competition to determine who would lead the issue.
But a Central Bank official on Thursday denied any such competition had been called.

Bank officials have said total issue of bonds would be $250 million dollars, with a first package of $50 million. The Eurobonds would have a maturity of between three months and a year and a yield of between 12 to 14 percent annual.
A top adviser to President Leonid Kuchma said last month that the first issue of bonds would be cautious and short-term to win the confidence of the international financial community.
Subsequent issues, he said, could be medium and long-term.

Central Bank governor Viktor Yushchenko has said that a bond issue next year is a vital part of the government's strategy to maintain its budget deficit at 3.8 percent -- 2.4 percent by Western methods of calculation.
He also said that several Western companies had already made enquiries about acting as an agent. --Natalia Zinets, Kiev newsroom +380 44 229 2264
